newsitem.title: USA: GM, Chrysler continue buying palladium, platinum.
newsitem.headline: GM, Chrysler continue buying palladium, platinum.

text.p: General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp said Thursday they have not made any changes in their purchases of palladium or platinum, despite sharply higher prices driven by concern about Russian supplies.
The automakers use the precious metals in catalytic converters for car and truck exhaust systems. A spokesman for Ford Motor Co was not immediately available for comment on its purchase plans.
"There has been no change in any of our long-term strategies, how we buy it and the amounts we buy," said Thomas Klipstine, a spokesman for GM's global purchasing group in Warren, Mich.

Klipstine said GM buys palladium and platinum from several sources, and sometimes varies its purchases according to the market, but he added that the company has not recently had any major shifts in its purchasing patterns.
GM's Delphi Energy & Engine Management Systems Division, the world's largest producer of automotive catalytic converters, also recovers some of the metals from recycling efforts, Klipstine said.
Chrysler spokesman Bryan Zvibleman said the automaker is continuing to buy palladium and platinum for its principal catalytic converter supplier, Johnson Matthey Plc.

Zvibleman also said that Chrysler has adequate supplies of the metals stockpiled to meet its near-term production needs. "We're not concerned by the situation in Russia because we have other sources to get it," he said.
AlliedSignal Inc, a major U.S. producer of catalysts, also has not altered its purchases, a company spokesman said Thursday, adding that market price fluctuations are normally passed on to customers.
Platinum and palladium prices have risen sharply in the last two months on worries about Russian supplies.

Annual supply talks between Russia and Japan broke down in December and Russian exports were cut off, pushing prices higher on concerns about smaller supplies and that the Japanese would be forced to bid for metal from other origins.

But Russian deliveries of palladium and platinum to Japan may restart at the end of March or the beginning of April, the deputy chief executive of state precious metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport said on Thursday.
Japan is the world's leading consumer of palladium and Russia is the world's largest palladium supplier and a leading exporter of platinum.
